newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat, Presscrete shines.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat, Presscrete shines.

text.p: Singapore shares were mostly flat at the open on Monday with Presscrete debuting with a 20 percent gain over its initial public offer price (IPO).

Presscrete, a specialist engineering group, listed on the second board, hit a high of Singapore $0.37 (US$0.26) against its IPO price of S$0.30. Volume was a brisk 3.23 million shares after 40 minutes of trading.

Dealers said the stock was doing well as its IPO of 14 million shares, was small. Switch-gear maker SMB United, which listed last week, offered 103 million shares in its IPO. Early Monday SMB was trading one cent above its S$0.29 offer price.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index was easier by 1.11 points to 2,169.94. Volume was a meagre 11.36 million shares with 42 gainers and 39 losers.
"The market is very quiet and I do not expect it to go anywhere today," said an institutional dealer with a local brokerage.
Dealers said there was a dearth of market-moving factors and investors were more interested in Malaysian shares.
Early gainers included Transmarco, Metro and SIA foreign while Cerebos Pacific, Keppel Corp and Jardine Strategic were lower.
